faq.a: Sayyid is associated with the Arabic form سَيِّد, whose core sense is sayyid; master, lord.

faq.q: What is the origin of Sayyid?
faq.a: Sayyid is associated with Arabic. Sayyid is Arabic سَيِّد (Sayyid), meaning 'master, lord'.
Yes — the underlying form سَيِّد is Arabic.
Sayyid can occur in Muslim naming contexts, but it is better described as a Arabic-origin name used within some Muslim naming traditions than as an exclusively Islamic religious term.
Sayyid should not be classified as a Quranic personal name without a direct Quranic basis. The root س و د is Quranic, but Sayyid is not itself a Quranic personal name.

faq.q: What does Sayyid mean in Urdu?
faq.a: In Urdu, Sayyid is rendered سید and carries the sense سید، سردار.

faq.q: What does Sayyid mean in Persian?
faq.a: In Persian, Sayyid is rendered سید and carries the sense سید، سرور.
A romanized syllable approximation is sayyid. No IPA transcription is asserted because a verified phonetic transcription was not available.

faq.q: What are the variants of Sayyid?
faq.a: Romanization variants include Sayyid, sayyid. Script forms are سَيِّد, سید, सैयद.

faq.q: Is Sayyid a boy's or girl's name?
faq.a: Documented usage records this form as male. Gender is not inferred from the meaning of the word, and actual use may vary between communities.
